newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds tighten in Treasuries selloff.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds tighten in Treasuries selloff.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities sold off Thursday morning, sparked by a selloff in Treasuries, but spreads over Treasuries narrowed somewhat, traders said.
"The (Treasury) market selloff induced mortgage-banker selling," said one trader, who added that the selling was "not huge size, pretty controlled."
Conventional 7.0- and 7.5-percent paper saw the most action, he said.
Some light midday buying helped tighten spreads, traders said.
By late afternoon, the market had settled with prices off 2/32 to 18/32 across the board.
"Right now it's completely dead," a trader said at 1500 EST/2000 GMT.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent pass-throughs were off 15/32 at 99-15/32, yielding 111 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were off 16/32 at 99-12/32 and 99-16/32, respectively.
The 10-year note had lost 24/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
